FragPunk brings a fresh twist to the hero shooter genre with its fast-paced gameplay, vibrant visual style, and unique Shard Card system that changes the rules of every match. The gunplay feels responsive, matches move at a thrilling pace, and the card mechanics create unpredictable moments that keep rounds exciting.

At its core, FragPunk has all the ingredients of a standout competitive shooter. The weapons feel satisfying, the characters are distinctive, and the constant gameplay variety helps it avoid feeling repetitive.

Unfortunately, the game's biggest weakness is its apparent reliance on bots. Many players have reported matches that feel filled with AI-controlled opponents rather than real competitors. Whether these bots appear in beginner lobbies, casual matchmaking, or other situations, their presence can make victories feel hollow and raise questions about the competitive integrity of the experience.

When you're matched against real players, FragPunk shines. The strategic use of Shard Cards combined with quick gunfights creates some genuinely memorable moments. However, it's difficult to fully invest in the competition when you're unsure if the enemy team is made up of actual players or scripted bots.

Despite this issue, the game remains fun for those seeking a casual shooter with a unique identity. The foundation is solid, and if the developers continue improving matchmaking transparency, FragPunk could become a much stronger competitor within the hero shooter market.

Pros
- Fast and engaging gunplay
- Creative Shard Card system
- Stylish visuals and presentation
- Matches rarely feel repetitive

Cons
- Bots can make matches feel artificial
- Competitive experience lacks trust and consistency
- Victories sometimes feel less rewarding

Final Score: 7/10
FragPunk is a creative and entertaining shooter with excellent gameplay foundations, but the perception of bot-filled matches prevents it from reaching its full potential. Great ideas and plenty of fun are here, but the multiplayer experience needs more authenticity to ensure long-term success.

[h1]I rarely leave reviews on Steam since I find them pointless. But these reviews are too harsh for a f2p game.[/h1] 

Now...

[b]My hands are full with FragPunk, shilling and defending this game 100%, putting my full support behind it. As of September 2026.[/b]

Nowadays, people love to hate games for any reason, disregarding the work of everyday programmers, artists, and player support agents. The problem!! greedy executives, stockholders, and lawyers who want to milk every penny from this industry.

I was pleasantly surprised with FragPunk, and above all, it's a 100% free game with cosmetic skins and almost no pay-to-win (some Operator unlocks, but these are mechanically complex / hard to play).

The developers and NetEase should keep it this way.

In my short time playing this game, I did encounter some problems that many have already pointed out:

[h3]Player Population-[/h3]
Sluggish matchmaking - A bigger player pool would fix this.
Cheaters (just two in my playtime) - Since it's a game from NetEase, this is mostly handled by the latter, not the game developers.
Bots - A bigger player pool would fix this.
Overall, this is 100% on both the publisher and developers, mostly due to marketing.

[h3]Gameplay / UI / UX-[/h3]
Extremely broken game modes - I actually liked this, but I understand why this would be a negative for a lot of people.
Unlocking some Operators / Heroes - Pretty self-explanatory.
Ranked mode extremely dependent on team play, team economy, team decisions, teamwork, team everything. It's ambitious, but people in most games hate to play in teams. Still, heavy team-oriented quirks define ranked, ESPECIALLY choosing card augments.
Card augments! - Cool. I would make them even crazier.
Overcrowded "mobile-first" UI/UX - A bunch of coins, materials, battle passes, chests, etc., etc. Very overwhelming.

[h3]Other-[/h3]
The art style is outdated and looks very generic / bland. I would simply go full generic and copy CoD / BF6 like all modern FPS games.

Found it fun with the overpowered mechanics, movement, and gunplay. Hope the devs can get more chances to fix the mess. 

My general advice is: "More streamlined and focused game."

FRAGPUNK was genuinely a lot of fun during Season 1. The gameplay was fast, chaotic and simply felt good. I actually enjoyed the game enough to spend money on it.

But the fact that you cannot disable crossplay on PC and are basically forced to play against players on other platforms using aim assist is honestly ridiculous.

In a competitive shooter, PC players should at least have the option to choose whether they want to play against controller players or not. Playing with mouse and keyboard against aim assist can feel incredibly unfair, especially when the game is supposed to be competitive.

The game also feels completely different compared to Season 1, and unfortunately not in a good way.

At this point, I honestly feel like the money I spent on this game was wasted.

Admittedly, I really enjoy Fragpunk! The game is oddly overstimulating with the powerful and brightly coloured visuals seemingly SHOUTING at you through the screen.. the UI seems like wayyyy to much when you're just starting ( you are faced with an army of red exclamation points), however, looking past all that shimmer and shine, you see a game which really tries to stand apart from the regular shooter scene, which I suppose also lead to its sadly small player base.

 I see a lot of people complaining that the real reason Fragpunk fell off is because it just tries to do too much, being a Hero shooter is great but adding the Shard cards makes it a whole new game, and that game is of course Fragpunk, there is a lot of discourse about the execution of this idea and I think people are just overwhelmed. Oddly enough, I enjoy it, for example, I tried FINALS and that game was too much for me, whereas Fragpunk felt like a breath of fresh air! Funky, colourful, fun!!  Having an oddly toxic relationship with shooter games like Valorant, this game doesn't feel that serious, and a shooter game that isn't really that serious is hard to come by.

 Fragpunk for me is a chill game where you basically just take the piss, the shooting feels really smooth, headshots feel great and if you understand hero shooters, you will understand Fragpunk, the shard cards just add a fun spin to it. And well of course the use of AI is horrible, and I don't support it at all, and in all fairness I have no idea how big their dev team is, but with their lack of advertising, it almost seems like they are leaning into the games death. Sadly, the queue times are a bit of a downer sometimes, but we digress..

The game is shamefully addictive for me and if you're looking for a stupid hero shooter with a stupid spin on it, this game is for you!

I honestly love this game. FragPunk has been a lot of fun, especially because the cards give every match a different feel. It keeps the game from getting crazy repetitive, and every game can play out differently. You get the occasional sus shot here and there, but overall I have a great time playing it.

I started playing solo once in a while, and I finally got one of my friends to try it. Now we have been playing nonstop for the last two weeks. i got a group together so much more fun, Once you get a group together, this game is seriously fun.

I did run into an issue trying to connect my accounts between PS5 and Steam. I can't get my account onto my PS5. I'm not sure if I messed something up by trying to connect everything through the game first, but hopefully this can be fixed because I would really like to play on both.

My biggest complaint is the pricing.

The battle pass is expensive, and the credits are pretty crazy too. I ended up getting the monthly option because I wanted to support the game and get the upgraded battle pass, but by the time everything is added up, I'm spending over $20.

I don't mind spending money on a game I enjoy. I actually WANT to support the developers because me and my group have been having a great time. But I think the prices are going to hurt the game in the long run.

If you want FragPunk to have longevity, I really think lowering the prices would help. More reasonable prices could mean more people buying things, more players sticking around, and more players coming back season after season.

I also really think there should be a rotating skin shop, or some way to buy skins that you missed. It is honestly pretty annoying seeing some really cool skins and characters locked behind a battle pass and knowing you might never be able to get them again.

Gameplay wise, FragPunk reminds me more of Halo than CS:GO or Valorant. It feels more forgiving when moving and shooting, and I personally really like that. It makes the game feel more fun and less punishing while still having plenty of skill involved.

Overall, I really enjoy FragPunk and I want to see this game succeed. The cards, gunplay, characters, and overall gameplay make it something I keep coming back to. Me and my friends have been having a blast.

Devs, if you really care about the longevity of the game, please take another look at the pricing and how skins are sold. Give players more reasonable prices and more ways to get the skins they actually want. I honestly think you'll keep more players around that way.

Great game. Just please don't price your players out of it.

Frag punk is a game that had and holds a very good potential in the FPS community however they hold very little control on the communities inner circles of the game whether it be matchmaking in general, cheaters, or games being thrown there is little to no repercussions for those actions despite the report system and the "anti cheat" that holds everything together. Understandably with a very small dev team they can only do so much but you cant expect people to influence a faulty work in progress game that has made it this far with little in-game work outside of graphic designs funneled through AI and a bias group of testers. At times its a very fun game but with little to no real safety net, shots that do not register despite hit marker implications and sound queues, high ranked individuals smurfing low elo on alternate accounts, cheaters on console and pc going unbanned by manipulating the K/D system, alongside no real balancing of lancers, its hard to give frag punk the over due credit of being the amazing game it could've been .
